questions.stem: A 68 year old man has 4 weeks of itching, dark urine and pale, greasy stools. He has no abdominal pain. He has smoked 30 cigarettes a day for 45 years and has lost 6 kg. questions.stem: A 76 year old man has 3 weeks of jaundice and itching without pain. His temperature is 36.8°C, pulse rate 74 bpm and BP 132/80 mmHg. On examination there is a smooth, non-tender, pear-shaped mass below the right costal margin that moves with respiration.

questions.stem: A 67 year old man with pancreatic adenocarcinoma has recurrent superficial thrombophlebitis at different sites and a recent DVT. His platelet count and clotting screen are normal. His pulse rate is 84 bpm and BP 128/78 mmHg. A student asks why his blood clots so easily.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
questions.e: Trousseau's syndrome is a hypercoagulable paraneoplastic state driven by tumour-derived tissue factor and mucin. Inherited thrombophilias are not linked to the cancer.

questions.stem: A 66 year old man has a pancreatic head tumour that obstructs the main pancreatic duct. He has pale, bulky stools that float. His temperature is 36.8°C, pulse rate 76 bpm and BP 128/80 mmHg. His faecal elastase is 62 µg/g (>200). A student asks what causes his stools.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of his stools?
o: Bacterial overgrowth in the small bowel
Bile acid malabsorption in the terminal ileum
Reduced pancreatic lipase reaching the duodenum
questions.e: Steatorrhoea results from reduced pancreatic lipase reaching the duodenum, shown by a low faecal elastase. Pancreatic enzyme replacement treats it.
